answer: A stake-weighted reputation ladder works like a terrace: each level up requires locking more collateral for longer, so a Sybil farm must fund every fake identity separately. The delta between a cheap throwaway account and a trusted one is measured in real cost and time, and anyone caught cheating loses the stake. That forges a simple rule — influence must be bought with commitment, not copied for free — which prices mass fakery out of the market.
